rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.6 describe a two-year (2013-2014) split-split-plot field experiment at Tarsus, Turkey, with four replications, comparing surface drip and subsurface drip under two frequencies and four regimes. Q2: Section 3.1 and Table 1 report that SDI plots received slightly less irrigation water (e.g. 216-418 mm vs 229-444 mm in 2014) and had slightly lower ETa than surface drip; Section 3.4 and Table 1 report WP and IWP by system, with the highest WP in SDI IF3 DI50 (21.9 and 24.5 kg m-3) and Table 3 showing a significant irrigation-system effect on WP in 2014 (P=0.008) and on IWP in 2014.
rows.notes: Own evidence concerns water applied, ETa and WP under SDI vs surface drip; the reduced evaporation explanation is asserted (Section 3.1 'due to reduced evaporation losses'), not measured, and deep drainage was assumed negligible, so Q4 is no. Single site, single crop, plot scale. Q7: the authors recommend against 6-day intervals with moderate/high deficit and state high WP should go with acceptable yield, but these are framed for yield/quality rather than as requirements for the SDI water-saving/WP effect, so no. Q8: no explicit limitations of own results stated. Q9: only LSD values and letter groupings (Tables 1, 3, 4), no SD/SE/CI for WP. Note the system effect on WP was ns in 2013 and the abstract's 'highest WP in SDI IF6 DI50' conflicts with Table 1 (SDI IF3 DI50).

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.6 describe a two-year replicated field experiment comparing surface and subsurface drip on eggplant.
rows.notes: The study reports no data on weeds, pests or diseases under SDI; weed and disease reduction is mentioned only in the Introduction as a reported advantage of SDI citing Lamm and Camp (2007) and Irmak et al. (2016). The study's own results concern irrigation amounts, ETa, soil water, yield, quality, WP and net income.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.6, two-year split-split-plot field experiment with four replications at Tarsus, Turkey. Q2: Section 3.3, Tables 1, 3 and 4 report that surface drip gave significantly higher yield than SDI in 2013 (65.6 vs 59.8 t ha-1; 7.3 and 11% higher for 3- and 6-day frequency) while the two systems did not differ significantly in 2014 (80.6 vs 80.0 t ha-1, ns); the authors note their result contradicts the Tunisian study of Douh and Boujelben (2010). Q4: Section 2.4 and 3.2, Figs 2-3 report neutron-probe soil water storage in the 60 cm root zone separately for DI and SDI plots, and Section 3.1/Table 1 report ETa by system, with lower water consumption under SDI linked to lower plant height (Table 2); Fig 4 gives yield-ETa relations for each system. Q7: Conclusions state that 3-day frequency with full irrigation is recommended under both systems to obtain higher yield and that longer intervals with moderate-to-high deficit are not recommended for SDI/DI eggplant, and that water management is critically important to obtain higher yields.
rows.notes: Yield measured by one method (hand harvest of centre rows), so Q3 no. One site, one crop, one cultivar, two seasons, plot scale (Q5, Q6 no). Q7 is borderline: the frequency/regime condition is stated as a recommendation drawn from own findings rather than an explicit requirement. Q8: no explicit limitations of own results beyond noting few comparative SDI-DI eggplant studies. Q9: only LSD and letter groupings (Tables 1, 3, 4), no SD/SE/CI for yields.

notes: Full text appears complete. Some data-entry inconsistencies in the tables (e.g. Table 2 TSS value of 90 for SDI IF6 PRD50 in 2014; Table 4 2014 interval means given as 8338 and 7723 rather than ~83380 and ~77230; abstract and Section 3.4 disagree on which SDI DI50 frequency had the highest WP).
